alignment.title: Use Alignment for your search
alignment.description: If you have completed Founder Alignment, you can prioritize up to three areas and say whether you prefer similarity there or welcome a different perspective.
alignment.choose: What matters most to you in a co-founder?
alignment.chooseHelp: Choose up to three areas. These cues are not hard filters and do not affect profile order or visibility.
alignment.unavailable: Complete Founder Alignment first. Your search works fully without Alignment signals.
alignment.transparency: Your selection stays private. A cue is only produced with bilateral sharing and sufficient responses.
alignment.disclaimer: These cues describe similarities and differences in your stated preferences. They do not predict whether you will work well together or build a successful company.

ownContext.title: Your starting point
ownContext.description: Your previous answers currently sit more in the “{tendency}” range.
ownContext.note: This is not an evaluation. In your search, you decide whether you prefer a similar perspective here or are open to difference.

company_logic.body: A similar overall direction can make it easier to carry priorities and strategic decisions together. Different views can reveal additional options, but they require clear conversations about what you are building toward together.
company_logic.conversation: Clarify early which goals are negotiable for each of you—and which are not.

decision_logic.body: Founders differ in how quickly they decide, how much alignment they expect and when individuals should act autonomously. Different preferences can work when decision rights and check-in points are clear.
decision_logic.conversation: Define which decisions individuals may make and which ones you make together.

work_structure.body: Different working styles can bring different strengths into a team while also creating additional coordination needs.
work_structure.conversation: Discuss communication rhythm, availability, focus time and expectations for collaboration.

commitment.body: Different expectations around time, priority and commitment can become especially relevant for founders. Difference is not automatically a useful complement here.
commitment.conversation: Clarify the effort you expect over the coming months and when changes should be renegotiated.

risk_orientation.body: Different risk thresholds can bring several perspectives to opportunity and safeguards. They can also make decisions more difficult.
risk_orientation.conversation: For larger or hard-to-reverse decisions, shared criteria, bounded experiments or external expertise can help.

conflict_style.summary: Raising tension and navigating difficult conversations.
conflict_style.body: People differ in whether they address tension immediately, need distance first or prefer to structure conflict factually. Differences need not be a problem, but they can lead to recurring misunderstandings.
conflict_style.conversation: Clarify how you notice that something should be discussed and what each person needs for a difficult conversation to remain possible.
